paragraphs.title: A Request for Examination and Separation from Evil

answers: The evildoers
The LORD
The congregation
easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “Judge me, O LORD.”
easy.q: Who does the psalmist ask to judge him?

answers: In the LORD
In vain persons
In his own strength
easy.explanation: He says, “I have trusted also in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist say he has trusted?

answers: People who walk in truth
Those who worship at the altar
Vain persons, dissemblers, and the wicked
easy.explanation: He says that he has not sat with vain persons and will not sit with the wicked.
easy.q: From whom does the psalmist separate himself?

answers: People devoted to truth
People characterized by emptiness or deceit
People serving at the altar
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to people from whom the psalmist separates himself because of their ungodly character.
medium.q: What does the phrase “vain persons” most nearly mean in this passage?

answers: To show that walking in truth includes avoiding evil company
To explain how the altar was built
To introduce the subject of thanksgiving
medium.explanation: His separation from deceitful and wicked people is presented as part of his faithful way of life.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist describe his separation from evildoers after speaking of his integrity and truth?

answers: Love for God’s house, thanksgiving, and then a request for judgment
A request for examination, a declaration of truth, and separation from the wicked
A plea for mercy, standing in an even place, and public blessing
medium.explanation: The psalmist first asks the LORD to examine him, declares his trust and truth, and then describes his avoidance of wicked people.
medium.q: What is the general progression in verses 1–5?

answers: Only his outward actions
Only his relationships with evildoers
His reins and his heart, meaning his inward thoughts and motives
challenge.explanation: He asks the LORD to “try my reins and my heart,” referring to his inner self.
challenge.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to examine according to verse 2?

answers: The psalmist approaches the LORD in confidence and places his life before Him
The psalmist asks the evildoers to judge him
The psalmist shows that he does not trust the LORD
challenge.explanation: His request for examination is made alongside the declaration, “I have trusted also in the LORD.”
challenge.q: What is the relationship between trusting the LORD and asking Him to judge the psalmist?

answers: The altar versus the congregation
Walking in integrity and truth versus keeping company with deceit and wickedness
Thanksgiving versus a request for mercy
challenge.explanation: The psalmist contrasts his faithful walk with the character and company of vain and wicked people.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in verses 1–5?

paragraphs.title: Purity, Thanksgiving, and Love for God’s Dwelling

answers: His hands
His house
The congregation
easy.explanation: He says, “I will wash mine hands in innocency.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he will wash in innocency?

answers: The congregation of evildoers
The altar of the LORD
The dwelling of the wicked
easy.explanation: He says, “so will I compass thine altar, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he will compass after washing his hands?

answers: The congregation of evildoers
The place of bribes
The habitation of God’s house and the place where His honour dwells
easy.explanation: He declares, “I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he loves?

answers: A dwelling place
A bribe
A level path
medium.explanation: A habitation is a dwelling or place of residence; here it refers to God’s house.
medium.q: What is the meaning of “habitation” in the phrase “the habitation of thy house”?

answers: To describe the bloody men
To give thanks to God and proclaim His marvelous works
To avoid the altar of the LORD
medium.explanation: The verse connects thanksgiving with declaring all of God’s wondrous works.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist wish to publish with the voice of thanksgiving and tell of God’s wondrous works?

answers: Purity is presented as preparation for approaching the LORD’s altar
Purity prevents the psalmist from approaching the altar
Purity concerns only those who accept bribes
medium.explanation: The psalmist speaks of washing his hands in innocency and then approaching the LORD’s altar.
medium.q: How does the washing of the hands relate to approaching the altar?

answers: Bribes, mischief, and then separation
Purity, approach to the altar, thanksgiving, and love for God’s dwelling
Examination, trust, and walking in truth
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from clean hands to the altar, thanksgiving, proclamation, and love for God’s house.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 6–8?

answers: He wants to avoid it
He sees it as connected with God’s presence and honor
He considers it a gathering place for evildoers
challenge.explanation: He loves the place because it is where God’s honour dwells.
challenge.q: What does the psalmist’s love for the habitation of God’s house reveal about that place?

answers: They are two expressions of praise directed toward God
They are presented as opposites
They concern only separation from the wicked
challenge.explanation: The psalmist joins thankful praise with proclaiming all the LORD’s wondrous works.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between thanksgiving and telling of God’s wondrous works?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Deliverance and Standing on the Straight Path

answers: Sinners and bloody men
Those who give thanks
Those who love God’s house
easy.explanation: He asks, “Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men.”
easy.q: With whom does the psalmist ask that his soul not be gathered?

answers: Thanksgiving
Bribes
Water
easy.explanation: The verse says, “their right hand is full of bribes.”
easy.q: What is full in the right hand of the wicked men described in verse 10?

answers: Redemption and mercy
Bribes and mischief
Separation from truth
easy.explanation: He says, “redeem me, and be merciful unto me.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask for after declaring his integrity?

answers: A place filled with bribes
A level and stable path
A gathering of evildoers
medium.explanation: An even place is level and secure; figuratively, it describes a steady and upright way.
medium.q: What does “an even place” mean in the phrase “My foot standeth in an even place”?

answers: He describes standing in an even place and blessing the LORD among the congregations
He returns to describe the bloody men
He returns to sit with the wicked
medium.explanation: After asking for redemption and mercy, he speaks of standing securely and blessing the LORD.
medium.q: What follows the psalmist’s request for redemption and mercy?

answers: To describe the wicked character of those from whom he seeks deliverance
To praise the actions of the wicked
To explain his love for God’s house
medium.explanation: Mischief and bribes characterize the bloody men with whom he does not want to be gathered.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist mention mischief and bribes?

answers: It reinforces his testimony that he is committed to an upright way
It shows that he has turned to sin
It describes the behavior of the bloody men
challenge.explanation: By saying again, “I will walk in mine integrity,” he emphasizes his continued commitment to an upright life.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the psalmist’s repeated reference to walking in integrity?

answers: It presents the psalmist as isolated from all worshippers
It presents him standing securely and praising the LORD among the worshipping assembly
It returns him to the company of those who accept bribes
challenge.explanation: The conclusion pictures him on a secure path, blessing the LORD among the congregations.
challenge.q: How does the ending, “in the congregations: I will bless the LORD,” complete the plea for deliverance?

answers: Bloody men, mischief, and bribes versus the psalmist’s integrity and secure standing
The altar versus the habitation of God’s house
Thanksgiving versus telling of wondrous works
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts corrupt and violent people with the psalmist’s integrity, redemption, and worship.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in verses 9–12?
